title: Organic Chemistry: Alkanes, Alkenes and Alcohols
seo_title: Year 12 A Level Chemistry: Organic Chemistry Worksheets
standard_text: Nomenclature and isomerism, alkanes and fuels, halogenoalkanes and nucleophilic substitution, alkenes and electrophilic addition, alcohols and their oxidation, and polymers.
meta_desc: Free Year 12 A level chemistry worksheets on organic chemistry: IUPAC names, general formulae, combustion, free-radical substitution, electrophilic addition, nucleophilic substitution and alcohols. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Name from the longest chain; number for the lowest locant.
key_sub: Primary alcohol → aldehyde → acid; secondary → ketone.
body_html:
How to think about it

Name compounds from the longest carbon chain (meth-, eth-, prop-, but-, pent-, hex-) and number from the end that gives the substituent or functional group the lowest number. Alkanes are CnH2n+2, alkenes CnH2n.

Alkanes react with halogens by free-radical substitution; alkenes undergo electrophilic addition; halogenoalkanes undergo nucleophilic substitution (aqueous OH⁻) or elimination (ethanolic OH⁻). Acidified dichromate oxidises primary and secondary alcohols (orange → green).

Example

Name CH₃CHBrCH₂CH₃.

4 carbons: butane

Br on C2

Answer: 2-bromobutane

Example

Moles of O₂ to burn 1 mol of C₃H₈?

3CO₂ + 4H₂O need 10 O atoms

Answer: 5

Common mistakes

  • Numbering from the wrong end of the chain.
  • Writing 'hydroxy' instead of the -ol suffix.
  • Thinking tertiary alcohols are oxidised.

faq.a: An electrophile is attracted to the electron-rich C=C double bond and adds across it, as with Br₂ or HBr.

faq.q: How do you tell primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols apart?
faq.a: Warm with acidified potassium dichromate: primary and secondary turn it green, tertiary do not.

items.q: Which test shows that a compound is an alkene?
c: bromine water turns from orange to colourless
items.e: Bromine adds across the C=C.

items.q: What type of mechanism happens when bromoethane reacts with aqueous NaOH?
items.e: OH⁻ attacks the δ+ carbon.

items.q: Which carbocation is the most stable?
items.e: Alkyl groups push electrons towards the positive carbon.

items.q: In free-radical substitution, which step makes two radicals from one molecule?
items.e: Cl₂ → 2Cl• in UV light.

items.q: Which alcohol can be oxidised to a ketone?
items.e: Secondary alcohols give ketones.

items.q: What forms when bromoethane is heated with ethanolic KOH?
items.e: In ethanol, OH⁻ acts as a base.

items.q: Which alcohol forms a carboxylic acid when heated under reflux with excess acidified dichromate?
items.e: Primary alcohols are oxidised to aldehydes and then acids.

items.q: How do catalytic converters remove carbon monoxide and NO?
items.e: A platinum or rhodium catalyst is used.

items.q: Why does a C=C bond prevent rotation and allow E/Z isomers?
c: it is weaker than a single bond
items.e: Each carbon of the C=C must have two different groups.

items.q: What catalyst is used to hydrate ethene to ethanol?
items.e: Steam and ethene at about 300 °C and 60 atm.

items.q: Which step of free-radical substitution removes radicals?
items.e: Two radicals join, for example Cl• + Cl• → Cl₂.

items.q: What colour change is seen when acidified potassium dichromate oxidises an alcohol?
items.e: Cr₂O₇²⁻ is reduced to Cr³⁺.

items.q: What is cracking?
c: separating crude oil by boiling point
breaking long-chain alkanes into shorter alkanes and alkenes
items.e: Thermal cracking gives many alkenes; catalytic cracking gives branched alkanes and aromatics.

items.q: How many structural isomers does C₅H₁₂ have?
items.e: Pentane, 2-methylbutane and 2,2-dimethylpropane.

items.q: Why are CFCs harmful to the ozone layer?
c: UV light makes chlorine radicals that break down ozone
items.e: One Cl• can destroy thousands of O₃ molecules.

items.q: Why is the C–I bond the most reactive carbon–halogen bond?
c: it has the lowest bond enthalpy
items.e: Bond strength matters more than polarity.

items.q: Why are addition polymers like poly(propene) hard to dispose of?
c: they are unreactive and not biodegradable
items.e: They are saturated with strong non-polar bonds.

items.q: What type of mechanism happens when bromine reacts with ethene?
items.e: The C=C bond is electron-rich and attracts electrophiles.

items.q: How many structural isomers does C₄H₁₀ have?
items.e: Butane and methylpropane.

items.q: What is the major product when HBr adds to propene?
items.e: It goes via the more stable secondary carbocation.
